cmp_aws.opportunity_interpretation: AWS represents a premier custom-silicon prospect with an existing multi-year collaboration intent covering Intel 18A and custom Xeon 6 processors on Intel 3, alongside massive ongoing deployment of proprietary Graviton, Trainium, and Nitro silicon. Beyond wafer manufacturing on Intel 18A and Intel 3, AWS's transition to four-chiplet architectures in Graviton5 and high-capacity HBM integration in Trainium3 and Trainium4 creates strong potential alignment for Intel Foundry's advanced packaging (such as EMIB 2.5D) and Accelerator Ecosystem Alliance design enablement. cmp_cerebras.opportunity_interpretation: Cerebras is a commercial fabless AI silicon company that relies exclusively on TSMC for 5nm wafer fabrication of its Wafer-Scale Engines and has disclosed risks around single-foundry dependence and delays in securing tape-out slots. While its proprietary whole-wafer architecture was co-developed with TSMC and explicitly avoids conventional CoWoS packaging and HBM, its need for geographic and foundry diversification—alongside roadmap plans to introduce 3D-stacked DRAM on future CS-6 wafers—presents a longer-term, high-complexity exploration opportunity for Intel Foundry and Advanced Packaging and Test. Any potential alignment would require deep technical validation to determine whether Intel's wafer manufacturing, 3D stacking, and high-density test platforms can accommodate Cerebras's unique wafer-scale integration requirements.

mappings.requirement: High-density 2.5D/3D heterogeneous advanced packaging and high-thermal-density testing for multi-chiplet and HBM integration.
mappings.rationale: Meta's MTIA architecture explicitly requires connecting multiple logic chiplets (compute, I/O, networking) with several HBM3e stacks in a single package, which directly matches Intel's EMIB 2.5D technology designed for shoreline-to-shoreline logic-to-logic and logic-to-HBM interconnects.

cmp_microsoft.custom_silicon_activity: Microsoft actively develops and deploys multiple multi-generational in-house custom silicon programmes for its Azure cloud infrastructure, including the Azure Maia AI inference accelerators (Maia 200 in full production on TSMC 3nm; Maia 300 announced with a multi-chiplet architecture on TSMC N2P and HBM4), Azure Cobalt Arm-based server CPUs (Cobalt 100 deployed globally; Cobalt 200 built on Arm Neoverse CSS V3 and TSMC 3nm), the Azure Boost Data Processing Unit (DPU), and the in-house Azure Integrated HSM security chip (open-sourced via Project Tessera). Additionally, Microsoft has stated plans to produce a chosen chip design on the Intel 18A process and secured IP rights to OpenAI's custom AI chip designs.
